clusters.label: Stone floor enclosures: natural and brick
Outdoor motifs: mountains, villages, ruins, and castles
clusters.notes: Row 1 is a mountain tile collection. Cells 1-2 are standalone mountains and cell 8 is blank. The remaining row-1 cells compose into large dynamic mountain constructions that can be layered and filled to build ranges, including volcano-like peaks. Reviewed against reference-overworld-dialogue-knight-marius.png.

collections.label: Grand open indoor door
collections.notes: Authored 2x2 doorway assembly built from four reusable open-door tiles.

collections.label: Grand closed indoor door
collections.notes: Authored 2x2 doorway assembly built from four reusable door tiles.

collections.label: Long indoor table
collections.notes: Three-part table kit with left / middle / right reuse semantics.

collections.label: Gold frame border kit
collections.notes: Border kit containing three related frame variants: a 3x3 border with open gaps and fancy corners, a 3x3 border with smooth joins and fancy corners, and a 2x2 border with simple corners that can pair with the middle connectors from either 3x3 variant.

collections.label: Ornate gap 3x3 frame
collections.notes: Reviewed ornate 3x3 frame family with visible connector gaps. Use as one coherent frame kit rather than mixing its connectors with the smooth family.

collections.label: Ornate smooth 3x3 frame
collections.notes: Reviewed ornate 3x3 frame family with smooth joins. Keep it distinct from the gapped ornate frame when authoring boxes.

collections.label: Less ornate gap 3x3 frame
collections.notes: Reviewed less-ornate 3x3 frame family with gap joins. This is one of the full-screen / large-panel frame families seen in the party-menu references.

collections.label: Less ornate smooth 3x3 frame
collections.notes: Reviewed less-ornate 3x3 frame family with smooth joins. This is the clean large-border family used for the party-menu outer shell.

collections.label: Menu cursor and square markers
collections.notes: Small UI controls used in party-menu style layouts. Keep the square markers and the right-pointing menu cursor easy to reach as separate runtime-facing aliases.

collections.label: Panel separator runs
collections.notes: Long separator runs used to divide portrait gutters, stat rows, and larger panel interiors. These compose with the frame families rather than standing alone.

collections.label: Party-menu row lead widgets
collections.notes: Short lead-in widgets used ahead of party-menu text rows and list markers inside the larger ornate frame.

collections.label: Indoor table kit
collections.notes: Shared indoor table kit. Legged pieces require their south edge to remain exposed and should therefore only appear on the bottom edge of a single composed table entity. Collection-level presets should represent one valid table entity at a time; multi-table dining clusters belong in scene or metatile presets instead.

collections.label: Low counter / shelf run
collections.notes: Standalone and left / repeatable middle / right run pieces for short counters or low shelving.

collections.label: Tall bookshelf run
collections.notes: Standalone and left / synthetic middle / right pieces for tall bookshelf runs. The middle slice is derived per variant from the left endcap tile so longer bookcase walls can be composed without inventing a new source-sheet cell.

notes: Current source-layout model: regions are the top-level ingest areas, clusters are bounded groups inside a region, tiles are individual grid cells inside those bounds, and collections describe larger logical constructs built from multiple cells.
For Minimal 8 specifically, the four visible source columns act as the top-level regions.
The canonical colored-background sheet is the first-pass evidence source for this layout, but the resulting tile semantics still live at family level.
